Enforce integer typing and indexes on hydrofabric id columns

Source: R/enforce_integer_ids.R
enforce_integer_ids.Rd

Normalizes a GeoPackage so identifier and topology columns are stored as INTEGER (not floating point) and the join keys are indexed. This keeps ids from serializing to scientific notation, shrinks them on disk, and speeds the toid-based joins the pipeline and downstream consumers rely on.

Usage

enforce_integer_ids(gpkg, layers = NULL, cast = TRUE, index = TRUE)

Arguments

gpkg

Path to a GeoPackage.

layers

Character vector of layers to process. NULL (default) processes every layer/table registered in gpkg_contents.

cast

Logical; retype integer-valued id columns to INTEGER. Default TRUE.

index

Logical; create indexes on id / toid join keys. Default TRUE.

Value

gpkg, invisibly.

Details

The cast is value-guarded: a column is retyped only when every non-null value is integer-valued. Prefixed string ids (fp-, cat-, nex-, ...) and genuine real-valued measures are therefore left untouched; only columns that really hold integers (reference COMIDs, hydrosequence, level paths, stream order, flags, ...) are converted.

Works entirely through SQL (no geometry is read into memory), so it is safe on the largest domains where materializing geometry would exhaust RAM.

Examples

# ids arriving as doubles are stored as INTEGER; prefixed string ids are not
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".gpkg")
con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), f)
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE flowpaths (flowpath_id TEXT, hydroseq REAL)")
#> [1] 0
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO flowpaths VALUES ('fp-1', 42.0)")
#> [1] 1
DBI::dbExecute(con, "CREATE TABLE gpkg_contents (table_name TEXT)")
#> [1] 0
DBI::dbExecute(con, "INSERT INTO gpkg_contents VALUES ('flowpaths')")
#> [1] 1
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

enforce_integer_ids(f)

con <- DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), f)
DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "PRAGMA table_info(flowpaths)")[, c("name", "type")]
#>          name    type
#> 1 flowpath_id    TEXT
#> 2    hydroseq INTEGER
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)
